profile.bio: I design experiences at the intersection of intelligent systems and spatial computing — intuitive, empathetic, and technically grounded. Over five years, I've delivered 20+ digital products across healthcare, enterprise, and education — from AI-driven dashboards and conversational interfaces to immersive VR therapy programs and luxury metaverse retail. I move fluidly between 2D UX and 3D interaction design, between research insight and shipped product. Currently completing an Executive Master's in Artificial Intelligence (GPA 4.0), sharpening the bridge between design craft and machine intelligence. Authorized to work in the U.S. on STEM OPT.

projects.title: Feed the Children — WebAR Donation Experience
projects.subtitle: XR · WebAR · Nonprofit
projects.blurb: A QR-triggered, browser-based AR pantry for Feed the Children — meet a real class, stock the shelves, and tap to donate, no app required.
projects.description: A web-based AR donation experience for Feed the Children, developed with the Truesense fundraising team. Scanning a code opens the browser and places a shoppable classroom pantry — stocked shelves, a real student roster, and a donate sign — right in the donor's room. Built on 8th Wall WebAR, handing off to the secure feedthechildren.org donation page.

details.challenge: Feed the Children needed a donation activation that made impact tangible — a dollar providing $9 of food and essentials felt abstract in a standard give flow, and an app download ahead of the donate button would kill conversion.
details.approach: Built the experience with 8th Wall WebAR: a printed QR magnet opens a 3D classroom food pantry placed on any surface, with drag-to-move interaction, openable cabinet doors, a real class roster with the kids' photos, and a hand-written 'Tap here to donate today' sign that hands off to the secure donation page.
details.result: A complete prototype journey — physical touchpoint to AR to donation page in a single flow — showing how a classroom shelf can become the ask itself, carried through Feed the Children's real brand and store imagery.

projects.imageAlt: Feed the Children WebAR donation experience on three phones

projects.title: Charm City Kings — HBO Max AR Face Filters
projects.subtitle: XR · Social · Campaign
projects.blurb: Instagram face filters and a street-name generator for HBO Max's first exclusive movie — fans claimed a Baltimore nickname and shared it.
projects.description: A social AR campaign for HBO Max's first exclusive movie, Charm City Kings. 'They call me…' Instagram face filters place the viewer in a polaroid frame and stamp a random street name — Mouse, Blax, Nicki, Holy Savage — over the shot, branded with the film's neon logo. Shipped with the streaming premiere campaign.

details.challenge: Charm City Kings premiered with no theatrical run, so awareness had to be earned in feeds. The campaign needed participatory, shareable content that put the movie's Baltimore world — nicknames, swagger, dirt-bike culture — into fans' own faces.
details.approach: Designed the 'They call me…' filter set: a polaroid-style frame with face tracking and a randomized street-name reveal, plus social media assets and promo cutdowns that kept one visual language from filter to feed.
details.result: Launched with the October 2020 premiere push — fans shared their filter selfies tagged with their new nicknames, turning every post into organic promotion for the film.

projects.imageAlt: They call me Holy Savage — Charm City Kings AR face filter frame

projects.title: Ascension Realty — AR Mobile Experience
projects.subtitle: XR · AR · Real Estate
projects.blurb: An AR mobile experience letting buyers scan a surface and walk through a full building — down to a single apartment — before it's ever built.
projects.description: An AR mobile experience built for a private real estate client, letting buyers scan a surface and walk through a full building, down to a single apartment, before it's ever built. Designed end-to-end in a three-week sprint.

details.challenge: A private real estate client had an early-stage idea — use AR to let buyers experience developments virtually — but with no clarity, no structure, and no defined user journey, under a three-week deadline and no existing app to reference.
details.approach: Owned concept, storyboard, asset direction, UX, interaction design, and sound. Built a city-to-room AR journey — scan a surface, then move from a city skyline to a tower to a floor plan to a single furnished room — sourcing and optimizing 3D assets and using Vuforia anchor points for stable tracking.
details.result: Delivered a functioning AR platform and a client-ready demo in three weeks, turning a rough idea into proof that AR belongs in real estate marketing.

projects.title: Interactive 3D
projects.subtitle: UX · Spatial
projects.blurb: Real-time interactive 3D — spatial interaction models, lighting, and motion prototyped for the web, built to feel native rather than gimmicky.
projects.description: An exploration of real-time interactive 3D on the web — prototyping spatial interaction models, lighting, and motion tuned for performance, to find the patterns that make 3D feel like a native part of an interface rather than a novelty.

details.challenge: 3D on the web often feels gimmicky — latency, missing affordance, and heavy assets break presence and make it feel bolted-on.
details.approach: Prototyped real-time 3D environments, iterating on spatial interaction models, lighting, and motion to keep everything responsive and performant in the browser.
details.result: A set of reusable spatial interaction patterns for interactive 3D that feel native — turning 3D from a novelty into a usable medium.
